questions.question_text: A car travels 100 m in 10 s at constant speed. What is its speed?
questions.markscheme_answer: Speed = distance / time = 100 m / 10 s = 10 ms<sup>-1</sup>

questions.question_text: A ball is dropped from rest and falls for 3 s. How far does it fall? (g = 10 ms<sup>-2</sup>)
questions.markscheme_answer: s = ½gt² = ½ × 10 × 9 = 45 m

A projectile is launched at 30° above horizontal with initial speed 20 ms<sup>-1</sup>. Find the maximum height reached. (g = 10 ms<sup>-2</sup>)
questions.markscheme_answer: v_y = 20 sin(30°) = 10 ms<sup>-1</sup>. At max height, v = 0: h = v²/(2g) = 100/20 = 5 m

questions.question_text: Two balls are thrown simultaneously: Ball A is thrown upward at 15 ms<sup>-1</sup> from ground level, Ball B is dropped from 25 m height. When and where do they meet? (g = 10 ms<sup>-2</sup>)
questions.markscheme_answer: Position A: y_A = 15t - 5t². Position B: y_B = 25 - 5t². When they meet: 15t - 5t² = 25 - 5t² → 15t = 25 → t = 5/3 s. Height: y = 15(5/3) - 5(25/9) = 25 - 125/9 = 100/9 ≈ 11.1 m

questions.question_text: A 2 kg object experiences a net force of 10 N. What is its acceleration?
questions.markscheme_answer: a = F/m = 10/2 = 5 ms<sup>-2</sup>

questions.question_text: A 5 kg box rests on a horizontal surface. The coefficient of static friction is 0.4. What is the maximum horizontal force that can be applied before the box moves? (g = 10 ms<sup>-2</sup>)
questions.markscheme_answer: F_max = μN = μmg = 0.4 × 5 × 10 = 20 N

questions.question_text: A 3 kg object moving at 4 ms<sup>-1</sup> collides with a stationary 1 kg object. They stick together. Find their common velocity after collision.
questions.markscheme_answer: Conservation of momentum: m₁v₁ + m₂v₂ = (m₁+m₂)v. 3×4 + 0 = 4v → v = 3 ms<sup>-1</sup>

questions.question_text: A 2 kg block on a 30° incline is connected by a massless rope over a pulley to a hanging 3 kg mass. Find the acceleration of the system. (μ = 0.2, g = 10 ms<sup>-2</sup>)
questions.markscheme_answer: For hanging mass: 30 - T = 3a. For block: T - 2g(sin30° + μcos30°) = 2a. T - 10 - 0.2×2×10×0.866 = 2a. T - 13.46 = 2a. Solving: a = (30 - 13.46)/5 = 3.3 ms<sup>-2</sup>

questions.question_text: A rocket of initial mass 1000 kg ejects gas at 500 ms<sup>-1</sup> relative to the rocket at a rate of 5 kg/s. What is the initial acceleration of the rocket if it launches vertically? (g = 10 ms<sup>-2</sup>)
questions.markscheme_answer: Thrust = v_exhaust × dm/dt = 500 × 5 = 2500 N. Weight = 1000 × 10 = 10000 N. Net force = 2500 - 10000 = -7500 N (cannot lift off initially). If thrust exceeds weight: a = (F - mg)/m

questions.question_text: In a Wheatstone bridge, R₁ = 100 Ω, R₂ = 200 Ω, R₃ = 150 Ω. What value of R₄ balances the bridge? If the galvanometer has resistance 50 Ω and the bridge is supplied by 6 V, find the galvanometer current when R₄ = 250 Ω.

questions.question_text: A projectile is launched from the ground with an initial speed of 28.5 ms<sup>-1</sup> at an angle of 40° to the horizontal. Calculate the height of the projectile at point P (in meters) when it has traveled a horizontal distance of 20.0 m. (Use g = 9.81 ms<sup>-2</sup>)
questions.markscheme_answer:
Horizontal velocity: $u_x = 28.5 \cos(40^\circ) = 21.83 \text{ ms}^{-1}$.
Vertical velocity: $u_y = 28.5 \sin(40^\circ) = 18.32 \text{ ms}^{-1}$.
Time to reach 20.0 m: $t = \frac{20.0}{21.83} = 0.916 \text{ s}$.
Height at P: $y = u_y t - \frac{1}{2}gt^2 = 18.32(0.916) - 4.905(0.916)^2 = 16.78 - 4.12 = 12.66 \approx 12.7 \text{ m}$.

questions.question_text:
A car accelerates uniformly on a straight road with a positive velocity. Three statements are given:

I. The acceleration is constant.
II. The magnitude of the car's average speed is equal to that of its average velocity.
III. The magnitude of the distance travelled by the car is longer than its displacement.

Which statements are correct?
questions.markscheme_answer: A) I and II. Uniform acceleration means constant acceleration (I). On a straight road, distance equals displacement, so average speed equals average velocity (II). Statement III is incorrect.

questions.question_text: A rock is thrown vertically upwards from a cliff edge with initial speed u. It hits the ground with speed 2u. What is the total flight time?
questions.markscheme_answer: A) 3u/g. Time up: t₁ = u/g (v = u - gt, where v = 0). Time down: t₂ = 2u/g (v = gt, final speed = 2u). Total = u/g + 2u/g = 3u/g

questions.question_text: A student walks 900 m to school and 1100 m back home via a different route. What is the total distance and displacement?

Average speed $v = \frac{120,000}{13520} \approx 8.88 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.

questions.question_text: A rock dropped from a bridge takes 1.45 s to hit the water below. Calculate the height of the bridge in meters. (Assume g = 9.81 ms<sup>-2</sup> and ignore air resistance)

Height $s = 0 + \frac{1}{2}(9.81)(1.45)^2 \approx 10.3 \text{ m}$.

questions.question_text: A small ball is dropped from a cliff of height 45.0 m. How long does it take to reach the ground in seconds? (Use g = 9.81 ms<sup>-2</sup>)
questions.markscheme_answer:
Displacement $s = 45.0 \text{ m}$. Initial velocity $u = 0$.
Acceleration $a = 9.81 \text{ m s}^{-2}$.
$s = \frac{1}{2}at^2 \implies 45.0 = \frac{1}{2}(9.81)t^2$.
$t = \sqrt{\frac{90.0}{9.81}} \approx 3.03 \text{ s}$.

questions.question_text: A drone drops a package from a height of 120 m. What is the package's instantaneous velocity magnitude just before it hits the ground? (Use g = 9.81 ms<sup>-2</sup>)
questions.markscheme_answer:

Acceleration $a = 9.81 \text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Displacement $s = 120 \text{ m}$.
$v^2 = 0^2 + 2(9.81)(120) = 2354.4$.
Therefore, $v = \sqrt{2354.4} \approx 48.5 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.

questions.question_text: A cart rolling down an inclined plane passes point A with a velocity of 2.5 ms<sup>-1</sup>. A short time later, it passes point B with a velocity of 6.1 ms<sup>-1</sup>. If the distance between A and B is 8.0 m, calculate the acceleration of the cart.
questions.markscheme_answer:
Initial velocity $u = 2.5 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Final velocity $v = 6.1 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Distance $s = 8.0 \text{ m}$.
Using $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$, we have $6.1^2 = 2.5^2 + 2(a)(8.0)$.
$37.21 = 6.25 + 16a \implies 30.96 = 16a \implies a \approx 1.935 \text{ m s}^{-2}$.

questions.question_text: A ball rolling down a slope passes a point P with a velocity of 1.2 ms<sup>-1</sup>. It passes point Q with a velocity of 2.6 ms<sup>-1</sup>. If it took 1.4 s to go from P to Q, determine the distance PQ.
questions.markscheme_answer:
With constant acceleration, average velocity $v_{avg} = \frac{u+v}{2} = \frac{1.2 + 2.6}{2} = 1.9 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
The distance is $s = v_{avg} \times t = 1.9 \times 1.4 = 2.66 \text{ m}$.

questions.question_text: A stone is thrown vertically upwards with an initial velocity of 6.2 ms<sup>-1</sup> from a balcony 8.5 m above the ground. With what speed would it hit the ground? (Use g = 9.81 ms<sup>-2</sup>)
questions.markscheme_answer:
Let upwards be positive.
$u = +6.2 \text{ m s}^{-1}$. $a = -9.81 \text{ m s}^{-2}$.
The final displacement is $s = -8.5 \text{ m}$ (since it hits the ground below the starting point).
$v^2 = 6.2^2 + 2(-9.81)(-8.5) = 38.44 + 166.77 = 205.21$.
$v = \sqrt{205.21} \approx 14.3 \text{ m s}^{-1}$. Note the speed is the magnitude.

questions.question_text: A small rock is thrown vertically upwards with an initial velocity of 22 ms<sup>-1</sup>. Calculate the *later* time (in seconds) when its velocity magnitude is exactly 10 ms<sup>-1</sup>. (Use g = 9.81 ms<sup>-2</sup>)

questions.question_text: A skier starts from rest and slides 12.0 m down a slope in 4.0 s with constant acceleration. In what total time (in seconds) after starting will the skier acquire a speed of 18 ms<sup>-1</sup>?
questions.markscheme_answer:
First find acceleration: $s = u t + \frac{1}{2} a t^2 \implies 12.0 = 0 + \frac{1}{2} a (4.0)^2$
$12.0 = 8.0 a \implies a = 1.5 \text{ ms-1}^2$
Now find time to reach 18 ms-1: $v = u + at \implies 18 = 0 + 1.5 t \implies t = 12 \text{ s}$.

questions.question_text: A car moving at 35.0 ms<sup>-1</sup> slows uniformly to a speed of 15.0 ms<sup>-1</sup> in a time of 5.0 s. Determine the distance it moves exactly during the third second of this braking period (from t=2.0 s to t=3.0 s).
questions.markscheme_answer:
First find acceleration: $a = \frac{v-u}{t} = \frac{15.0 - 35.0}{5.0} = -4.0 \text{ ms-1}^2$
Distance at $t=3$: $s_3 = (35)(3) + 0.5(-4)(3)^2 = 105 - 18 = 87 \text{ m}$
Distance at $t=2$: $s_2 = (35)(2) + 0.5(-4)(2)^2 = 70 - 8 = 62 \text{ m}$
Distance in 3rd second = $s_3 - s_2 = 87 - 62 = 25 \text{ m}$.

questions.question_text: A stone is thrown straight upward with a speed of 24.0 ms<sup>-1</sup>. It is caught on its way down at a point 8.0 m above where it was thrown. How long did the entire trip take in seconds? (Use g = 9.81 ms<sup>-2</sup>)
questions.markscheme_answer:
Taking up as positive: $u = 24.0 \text{ ms-1}$, $a = -9.81 \text{ ms-1}^2$, $s = +8.0 \text{ m}$.
Using $s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2$:
$8.0 = 24.0t - 4.905t^2$
$4.905t^2 - 24.0t + 8.0 = 0$
Using quadratic formula: $t = \frac{24.0 \pm \sqrt{(-24.0)^2 - 4(4.905)(8.0)}}{2(4.905)} = \frac{24.0 \pm \sqrt{576 - 156.96}}{9.81} = \frac{24.0 \pm 20.47}{9.81}$
The two times are $0.36 \text{ s}$ (on the way up) and $4.53 \text{ s}$ (on the way down). The answer is $4.53 \text{ s}$.

questions.question_text: A baseball is thrown straight upward on the Moon with an initial speed of 30 ms<sup>-1</sup>. The acceleration due to gravity on the Moon is 1.62 ms<sup>-2</sup> downward. At what time (in seconds) is the ball at a height of 150 m while descending?
questions.markscheme_answer:
Up is positive. $u = 30$, $a = -1.62$, $s = 150$.
$s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2 \implies 150 = 30t - 0.81t^2$
$0.81t^2 - 30t + 150 = 0$
Quadratic formula: $t = \frac{30 \pm \sqrt{900 - 4(0.81)(150)}}{1.62} = \frac{30 \pm \sqrt{900 - 486}}{1.62} = \frac{30 \pm \sqrt{414}}{1.62} \approx \frac{30 \pm 20.35}{1.62}$
Ascending time: $t_1 \approx 5.96 \text{ s}$. Descending time: $t_2 \approx 31.08 \text{ s}$.
(Using exact values gives roughly 31.1 s depending on rounding). Let's use 31.1 s.

questions.question_text: A ballast bag is dropped from a hot-air balloon that is 250 m above the ground and rising steadily at 15.0 ms<sup>-1</sup>. What is the maximum height (in meters) reached by the bag above the ground? (Use g = 9.81 ms<sup>-2</sup>)
questions.markscheme_answer:
When dropped, the bag retains the balloon's upward velocity: $u = +15.0 \text{ ms-1}$.
At max height relative to release point, $v = 0$.
$v^2 = u^2 + 2as \implies 0 = 15.0^2 + 2(-9.81)s$
$s = \frac{225}{19.62} \approx 11.47 \text{ m}$ above release.

questions.question_text: A bag is dropped from a balloon that is 150 m above the ground and rising at 8.0 ms<sup>-1</sup>. How many seconds does it take for the bag to hit the ground? (Use g = 9.81 ms<sup>-2</sup>)
questions.markscheme_answer:
Taking up as positive and release point as $y=0$.
$u = 8.0 \text{ ms-1}$, $s = -150 \text{ m}$, $a = -9.81 \text{ ms-1}^2$.
$s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2 \implies -150 = 8.0t - 4.905t^2$
$4.905t^2 - 8.0t - 150 = 0$
$t = \frac{8.0 \pm \sqrt{(-8.0)^2 - 4(4.905)(-150)}}{9.81} = \frac{8.0 \pm \sqrt{64 + 2943}}{9.81} = \frac{8.0 \pm 54.836}{9.81}$
Choosing the positive root: $t \approx 6.40 \text{ s}$.

questions.question_text: A projectile is fired horizontally with a speed of 45.0 ms<sup>-1</sup> from the top of a cliff 120 m high. How far from the base of the cliff (in meters) will it strike the level ground? (Use g = 9.81 ms<sup>-2</sup>)
questions.markscheme_answer:
Vertical motion (find time): $s_y = u_y t + \frac{1}{2}a_y t^2$
$120 = 0 + 4.905t^2 \implies t = \sqrt{\frac{120}{4.905}} \approx 4.946 \text{ s}$
Horizontal motion: $s_x = u_x t = 45.0 \times 4.946 \approx 222.57 \text{ m}$.

questions.question_text: A cannonball is fired from a 60.0 m high cliff at an angle of 30.0° above the horizontal with an initial speed of 50.0 ms<sup>-1</sup>. Calculate the time of flight in seconds before it hits the sea below. (Use g = 9.81 ms<sup>-2</sup>)

Vertical components: $u_y = 50.0 \sin(30^\circ) = 25.0 \text{ ms-1}$.
$s_y = -60.0 \text{ m}$ (taking launch point as origin). $a_y = -9.81 \text{ ms-1}^2$.
$s_y = u_y t + \frac{1}{2}a_y t^2 \implies -60.0 = 25.0t - 4.905t^2$
$4.905t^2 - 25.0t - 60.0 = 0$
$t = \frac{25.0 \pm \sqrt{625 - 4(4.905)(-60.0)}}{9.81} = \frac{25.0 \pm \sqrt{625 + 1177.2}}{9.81} = \frac{25.0 \pm 42.45}{9.81}$
Taking the positive root: $t \approx 6.88 \text{ s}$.

questions.question_text: A speeder traveling at a constant 30.0 ms<sup>-1</sup> passes a hidden police car. Exactly 2.0 seconds after the speeder passes, the police car begins pursuit, accelerating from rest at 4.0 ms<sup>-2</sup>. How many seconds does it take the police car to catch the speeder (measured from the moment the police car starts moving)?
questions.markscheme_answer:
Let $t$ be the time the police car has been moving.
Distance traveled by speeder: $s_s = 30.0 \times (t + 2.0)$
Distance traveled by police: $s_p = \frac{1}{2} \times 4.0 \times t^2 = 2.0t^2$
Equating distances: $2.0t^2 = 30.0t + 60.0$
$t^2 - 15.0t - 30.0 = 0$
$t = \frac{15.0 \pm \sqrt{225 - 4(1)(-30)}}{2} = \frac{15.0 \pm \sqrt{345}}{2} = \frac{15.0 \pm 18.57}{2} \approx 16.79 \text{ s}$.

questions.question_text: A hot-air balloon is rising vertically at 12 ms<sup>-1</sup>. An object is thrown downwards from the basket with a velocity of 5 ms<sup>-1</sup> relative to the balloon. If it takes 4.0 s to hit the ground, what was the height of the balloon (in meters) when the object was thrown? (Use g = 9.81 ms<sup>-2</sup>)

Initial velocity of object relative to ground: $u = 12 \text{ (up)} - 5 \text{ (down)} = +7 \text{ ms-1}$ (upwards).

Displacement $s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2 = 7(4.0) + 0.5(-9.81)(4.0)^2 = 28 - 78.48 = -50.48 \text{ m}$.
The displacement is 50.48 m downwards, so the initial height was 50.5 m.

questions.question_text: Two balls are dropped to the ground from different heights. One is dropped 1.5 s after the other, but they both strike the ground at the exact same time, 5.0 s after the FIRST was dropped. questions.question_text: A high-speed train running along a straight track at 65.0 ms<sup>-1</sup> is slowed uniformly to a stop in 48.0 s. What is its stopping distance in meters?
questions.markscheme_answer:
Since acceleration is uniform, average velocity $v_{avg} = \frac{65.0 + 0}{2} = 32.5 \text{ ms-1}$.
Stopping distance $s = v_{avg} \times t = 32.5 \times 48.0 = 1560 \text{ m}$.
